text:
incident-bot: PAGER — high-severity alert for ACME private cluster: GPU node pool exhausting capacity; queue length > 1200 requests, token throttles reported. Auto-scaler failing to provision new nodes. Please ack and triage.

irene (eng-oncall): acked. paging SRE + runtime. taking lead.

matt (sre): looking at cluster metrics now — API shows GPU utilization ~98%, pods Pending=42, NodeProvision Errors=fetching image timed out for 6m. Kube events show 'Insufficient local SSD' on some nodes.

oleks (runtime): odd — autoscaler tried scale up to 12 but kept hitting node creation quota in customer cloud account. We see rate-limited responses from their cloud provider: HTTP 429 createInstances.

karen (support): on call with customer-ops now, they're seeing requests failing with 503 and long queue latencies. Customer reports degraded UX in production. ETA on node quota increases unknown.

raj (solutions): can we temporarily route ACME traffic to a hosted fallback model? We have policy to failover to hosted for critical customers but need approval and a config flip.

irene (eng-oncall): do it. prioritize customer availability. matt, coordinate failover. oleks, prepare small-model variant and CPU path in case GPUs not available.

matt (sre): starting failover procedure — updating routing policy to backup-hosted for acme:service-a. Applying policy patch now.

deploy-bot: applied route change to service-acme in prod (rev 202). Rolling update started.

customer-ops (acme): confirm receiving degraded but working responses — thanks for quick action. UX much better than full outage.

oleks (runtime): prepping a quantized 4-bit variant (gpt-small-q4) that runs on CPUs/GPU-less hosts for low-latency fallback. Building artifact, may take ~8–12 min.

matt (sre): autoscaler logs: "FailedScaleUp: quotaExceeded createInstances" repeated. Also saw a throttling backoff loop in our controller where we retried every 30s and then hit exponential backoff. That explains slow reaction to queue growth.

irene (eng-oncall): who has access to customer cloud console to request quota bump / expedite node provisioning?

karen (support): customer-ops says their cloud account team is investigating; they opened a support ticket with provider — ticket #CLOUD-9082. They estimate 1–2 hours.

raj (solutions): while we wait, suggest reducing per-request concurrency and enabling aggressive batching to keep costs and load down on fallback. Also enable per-tenant rate-limits to avoid noisy neighbors.

oleks (runtime): applying reduced concurrency and batch size for ACME route on hosted fallback. Snippet applied: ```json
{ "max_concurrency": 4, "batch_size": 8, "timeout_ms": 30000 }
```

matt (sre): queue length dropped from 1200 -> 320 after route flip and reduced concurrency. Error rate on ACME service down to 1.2% (was ~18%). Good.

irene (eng-oncall): capture customer impact for postmortem: outage window start 1793456789, major service degradation until routing flip at ~1793456940. Please log all actions.

customer-ops (acme): will collect user-facing metrics and open an incident review on our side; appreciate the handoff.

oleks (runtime): quick note — when autoscaler retried, it didn't respect provider-side 429 Retry-After header. We'll add handling to back off properly and avoid tight retry loops that make quota worse. Filing runtime ticket.

matt (sre): we manually provisioned 3 GPU nodes via provider console as a stop-gap — those nodes booted but two failed node init due to image pull timeouts. We moved some pods to succeed nodes. New nodes show taint "node.kubernetes.io/unavailable=false" now.

irene (eng-oncall): on-call handoff in 45m; matt will stay until cluster stabilized. I (irene) will write a summary and start a sev doc.

karen (support): action items for support: 1) follow up on CLOUD-9082, 2) update customer with ETA and mitigation steps, 3) send post-incident notes to ACME ops team.

raj (solutions): long-term: recommend customers run a small headroom config in private clusters (reserve 10–20% capacity) or enable our 'reserved burst' tokens on Dedicated to avoid total exhaustion. Also document steps for local quota escalations.

oleks (runtime): created ticket RUNTIME-2319: "Respect cloud 429 Retry-After and cap autoscaler retry rate; fallback to queued request shed policy when provisioning fails."

matt (sre): metrics check at 1793459800: queue steady ~150, CPU fallback healthy. We'll monitor for 2 more hours, then return control to normal routing if provider resolves quota.

deploy-bot: rollback capability staged for route change — can revert to private-cluster routing via console flag.

irene (eng-oncall): end-of-thread notes: severity reduced to SEV-2 after successful failover. Root cause: customer cloud-side instance quota + autoscaler retry behavior exacerbating provisioning delays + occasional image pull flakiness during node init.

incident-bot: incident update logged in tracker: INC-2026-1793456789. Postmortem requested by eng-sre.

customer-ops (acme): thanks all, we'll coordinate a joint postmortem.

irene (eng-oncall): assigning postmortem owners: matt (SRE) + oleks (runtime) + karen (support). Please include timeline, customer impact, mitigation steps, and long-term remediation.

matt (sre): acknowledged. beginning timeline capture now.

oleks (runtime): will add code-level patch for autoscaler and schedule canary.

karen (support): I'll handle customer comms and follow-up notes.

— end of thread —
